When Umar bin Abdul Aziz delayed a prayer, Urwa told him Gabriel had led the Prophet in the five prayers, and that Asr was prayed while sunshine lit Aisha's room.
In severe heat Zuhr is delayed until it cools and hillocks cast shadows, for intense heat is from Hell's raging; Hell was allowed two breaths, in summer and winter.
Abu Barza gave the Prophet's times, Zuhr at the sun's decline, Asr while the sun was hot and Isha late; Asr was prayed with sunshine still in Aisha's room.
Asr was prayed early enough to reach Quba or Al-Awali with the sun still high; whoever misses Asr is as if he lost family and property, his deeds annulled.
Whoever catches one rak'a of Asr before sunset, or of Fajr before sunrise, should complete the prayer.
Maghrib was prayed once the sun set, Isha early or late as people gathered and Fajr in darkness; Maghrib should not be called Isha as bedouins do.
With Isha delayed until people slept, the Prophet said none on earth but they awaited it, waiting counts as prayer, and but for hardship he would order it then.
Fajr began about fifty verses' recitation after the pre-dawn meal, in a darkness that hid veiled women; whoever catches one rak'a of a prayer in its time has caught it.
The Prophet forbade prayer after Fajr until the sun rises and after Asr until it sets, and at sunrise and sunset themselves; Ibn Umar forbade only those two moments.
Asr is hastened on cloudy days; Fajr missed in sleep was prayed after sunrise, Asr missed at the Trench after sunset, and a forgotten prayer is prayed when remembered.
The Prophet preferred Isha late and disliked talk after it, said those waiting for prayer are in prayer, and after Isha said none then alive would outlive a hundred years.
With the Prophet, Zuhr and Asr were prayed together as eight rak'at and Maghrib and Isha as seven, which the narrators thought meant delaying one prayer and advancing the other.
The Prophet prayed Asr while the sun still shone in Aisha's dwelling.
When the Prophet delayed the Isha prayer until women and children slept, he said he would order it at that hour were it not hard on his followers.
The Prophet prayed Asr early enough that one could reach Al-Awali, three or four miles away, while the sun was still high.
When the people overslept the morning prayer, the Prophet said Allah took their souls and returned them when He willed, and he prayed after the sun had risen.
